qualification.changedGraphReason: Three production modules changed. Their70 retained authored registrations were requalified against the changed graph, not counted from historical runs. Six source-pin guard sections changed; earlier scenario bodies and result artifacts are preserved. The pre-existing independent phase2a preimage encoder was admitted only as a pure node:crypto oracle, never its SDK/child-process harness.
qualification.keyObservedDifferential: The earlier field-only consumer accepts a correctly shaped draft with zero hash and a block whose nonce changed while its old hash remained. Both are rejected by the new hash path. An independently computed correct hash of a wrong recipient/payer/amount/asset/chain/account/ack/data/Plasma selection passes the raw hash checker but is rejected by the combined independent payment-and-price binding.
qualification.otherObservedBoundaries: All admitted current-price advances preserve the original unsigned-subject fields and pair; stale/current-policy/resource mismatches refuse. Hybrid selected50/108000 stays distinct from fusion-only total121. The fixture nonce is arbitrary and receives NO work verification. Public-key changes leave the hash unchanged under this encoding but change fieldDigest; key/address binding remains NOT_PERFORMED. Nonempty signatures refuse because this path is unsigned only.
qualification.independentCommitmentOracle: The retained independent306-byte encoder at test-support/phase2a-account-block-preimage.js is unchanged and matches immutable parent blob a6a48b0ea2f105a3bcc82c76fe02531eea18f8e0,7724B,SHA256 dde02531faaf3c45c5ab9760beba84fe56664f923c1d61fa64b077682d97dc0e. Its independently written byte/Bech32 encoding is compared with the new production path, including safe uint64/uint256 boundaries and field mutations. Both use the pinned Node builtin SHA3 implementation as a native premise; no SDK package or public chain oracle is executed.
qualification.abstractMethodExercise: Retained abstract prepareUnsigned() refusal checks stay unchanged. The new API checks an already supplied declared unsigned hash; it does not implement or invoke SDK prepareUnsigned/prepareBlock.

No source changed, import or native test occurred from that refused patch. It is retained separately and is not a passed assertion or test failure. One actual Node command passed all82 selected cases. Earlier metadata/loader failures remain in their own retained records.
